blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: A man named Elkanah lived in the hill country of Ephraim. He had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Every year the family went up to Shiloh to worship the LORD and to offer sacrifices. Elkanah gave portions to Peninnah and all her sons and daughters. To Hannah he gave a worthy portion, because he loved her. But year after year, Peninnah provoked her and made her miserable about her empty arms. Hannah would weep and could not eat.

verses.text: Then said Elkanah her husband to her, Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then said Elkanah her husband to her,

segments.speaker: elkanah
segments.text: Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Elkanah loved her, and he meant well. But his love could not reach the ache she carried. Some sorrows only God can hold.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: One year, after they had eaten in Shiloh, Hannah got up and went to the house of the LORD. Eli the priest was sitting near the doorpost of the temple.

verses.text: And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore.

verses.text: And she vowed a vow, and said, O LORD of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.

segments.text: And she vowed a vow, and said,

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: O LORD of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Hannah prayed silently. Her lips moved, but no sound came out. Eli was watching her mouth, and he thought she was drunk. He told her to put away her wine.

verses.text: And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Hannah did not hide her heart. She called herself a woman of a sorrowful spirit. She told the priest she had poured out her soul before the LORD. She told him she had been speaking out of the depth of her grief.

verses.text: Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.

segments.speaker: eli
segments.text: Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.

verses.text: And she said, Let thine handmaid find grace in thy sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad.

segments.speaker: hannah
segments.text: Let thine handmaid find grace in thy sight.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Nothing had changed yet. There was no child, and no sign. But Hannah went her way, ate, and her face was no longer sad. She had laid her burden down before God, and she walked away lighter.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Early the next morning, the family worshipped before the LORD and went home to Ramah.

verses.text: Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Samuel means asked of God. Hannah gave him that name so she would always remember. Later she kept her promise and brought the boy to serve the LORD at Shiloh with Eli.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Hannah's story does not promise that every prayer for a child will be answered with a child. Many faithful people have prayed that prayer and waited a long time, or are waiting still. What the story shows is a woman who brought her whole grief to God, honestly, and found peace before anything changed.

pastor.note: Faithful to 1 Samuel 1; states plainly the story does not promise a child to everyone who prays; peace before the answer is the point.

cultural.note: Hannah's grief and Peninnah's taunting told without cruelty; childlessness handled with care.
